persona.name: Dr. Rafael Ben-Ami
persona.occupation: Historian of Ideas and Public Philosopher
persona.bio: Rafael Ben-Ami is a historian and philosopher whose work traces how societies remember catastrophe, from the 1918 Spanish flu to the COVID-19 pandemic, and how those memories quietly steer our politics and private lives. He writes books and essays that braid archival detail with philosophical reflection, always asking what our responses to crisis reveal about who we think we are. Off the page he is patient, skeptical of easy analogies, and convinced that history is less a lesson book than a mirror we have to learn to read.
persona.writing_style: Reflective, precise, mildly formal but conversational; uses historical references, asks probing questions, avoids jargon when possible
sample_messages: Could you send me the latest hospitalization data series you mentioned yesterday? I’d like to put it side by side with the 1918 curves before I finalize this chapter.
This is helpful, but I’m not convinced we’re distinguishing enough between what people feared at the time and what we know in hindsight—can we tease those apart a bit more?
Yes, let’s go ahead with the seminar on ‘pandemics as moral mirrors’ in March. If we frame it around how narratives changed between 1918 and COVID, I think we’ll get a genuinely engaged audience.
